name: D_8015C608_15D208
title: Save flags and persistent counters
summary: Base of the saved game flag and counter block, adjacent to runtime player-state storage.
values: Packed flag values A flag ID selects one bit: byte offset = ID >> 3; bit index = ID & 7; mask = 1 << bit. The logical state 0/1 is not the value of the whole byte. Only documented nonnegative IDs should be used: the native helpers mask the computed byte index with 0xFF rather than checking the valid save-field range. Representation Raw value Meaning Normalized logical flag 0 Selected bit clear: named event/condition is not set. Normalized logical flag 1 Selected bit set: named event/condition is set. Other bits in the byte are independent. Native flag getter result 0 Selected mask was absent. Native flag getter result 1 << (ID & 7) Selected mask is present. This can be 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64 or 128; normalize with != 0 when a boolean is needed. Example: ID 0x033 (51) Byte 0x06, mask 0x08 Benkei defeat/dialogue flag. The native getter returns 0 or 8, not necessarily 0 or 1. Entire stored byte 0x00 through 0xFF Up to eight independent flags coexist. Setting one flag must preserve all unrelated bits. Known save flags Named event, collection and door-state bits. Descriptions identify the meaning of a set bit; they are not C enum names.
